title: Console UI: Route insights table + filters (Top cost drivers)
creator: Dylan Brooks
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
description:
Goal
Build the Usage Insights landing page in Console: a route-ranked table with first-class filtering, clear loading/empty/error states, and performance that holds up under high-cardinality orgs. This is the primary entry point for "What routes are costing us the most?" and should drive users into route detail (ENG-8427) and export (ENG-8425).

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/in-console-usage-insights-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-usage-insights-route-model-breakdown.json
- Cardinality guardrails: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/cost-attribution-cardinality-guardrails.json
- API contract: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-analytics-api-contract.json

Scope
1) Route insights table (Top routes by cost)
- Default sort: Total cost (descending)
- Columns (final names per Design):
  - Route (normalized display name + tooltip with full value)
  - Total cost (currency, includes cached tokens per metering rules)
  - Input tokens / Output tokens
  - Cached tokens (if available; else show —)
  - p95 latency
  - Error rate
  - Requests
  - Trend sparkline (time-series over selected range; can be a lightweight mini chart)
- Row click navigates to route detail view (ENG-8427), preserving filters in URL.
- Support "Unknown route" row with inline explanation + link to route-tagging docs (once ENG-8431 lands).

2) Filters + query state
- Filter bar (server-backed):
  - Time range selector (e.g., Last 24h / 7d / 30d + custom)
  - Environment (prod/staging/dev if available)
  - Region
  - Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
  - Org/project (in-console picker; respect existing Console scoping)
- Optional / behind flag if backend supports: Model filter for narrowing route list.
- Filters reflected in URL query params for shareability.
- Debounced filter changes; no client-side mega-aggregation.

3) Pagination + limits
- Server-side pagination (cursor or page/limit per API contract).
- Page size: 50 (default). Allow 25/50/100.
- Hard cap for UI browsing: maximum 500 routes returned across pages (beyond that show a guidance callout; see cardinality guardrails).

4) Loading / empty / error states
- Initial load: show skeleton table (header + 10 skeleton rows) within 200ms of navigation.
- Filter changes: keep prior table visible with subtle "updating" affordance (spinner in header) OR show per-row skeletons (final choice: per Design review).
- Empty state (no data for selection):
  - Message: "No usage data for this time range" + suggestion to widen time range.
  - Secondary: if route tagging missing, show "Most requests are missing route identifiers" with link to docs + instructions to update SDK.
- Error state:
  - Inline banner with retry
  - If 403/tenant scope issue: show permission copy and link to admin/RBAC doc.

Non-goals
- Implementing export UI beyond a placeholder action (ENG-8425 owns export job flow and download UX).
- Custom dimensions beyond route/model.
- Full anomaly detection.

Performance requirements (UI)
- Initial render (navigation -> meaningful content): p95 < 2.0s on typical orgs (50 routes, 7d range) on median laptop + normal network.
- Filter apply (interaction -> updated rows): p95 < 1.5s (assumes API p95 meets SLO).
- Table interactions (sorting, pagination controls) should not block main thread; avoid heavy chart libs for sparklines.
- Avoid re-render storms: memoize row components; virtualize only if needed (start without virtualization, add if perf regression found in dogfood).
- Query budget awareness:
  - Do not issue more than 1 in-flight list request at a time; cancel prior requests on filter change.
  - Cache last successful response per (scope + filters) for back/forward nav.

Implementation notes
- Gate behind feature flag: console.usage_insights_routes_v1
- API integration: use insights route list endpoint from ENG-8423.
- URL params: timeRange, start, end, env, region, deploymentMode, projectId, pageSize, cursor.
- Formatting:
  - Cost: currency formatting with 2 decimals, compact for large values (e.g., $12.3k) with tooltip exact.
  - Latency: ms; show — if insufficient samples.
  - Error rate: percent with 2 decimals; show — if zero requests.
- Accessibility:
  - Table headers are proper <th> with scope
  - Keyboard navigation for row click (Enter/Space)
  - Focus states visible, tooltips accessible (aria-describedby)

Acceptance criteria
- Route list page matches Design spec for layout (filter bar, table, row click behavior).
- Default sort by Total cost desc.
- Pagination works and preserves filters.
- URL is shareable and reproduces view on reload.
- Loading, empty, and error states implemented and reviewed by Design.
- Respects org/project scoping: no cross-project data shown when switching scope (verify with ENG-8428 test plan).
- Instrumentation: emit console event "usage_insights.routes.view" with dimensions (timeRangePreset vs custom, deploymentMode, hasData) and "usage_insights.routes.filter_change" (field name only; no raw route values).

QA / testing
- Unit tests: filter param parsing/serialization; currency/latency formatting.
- Integration tests: mocked API responses for empty/error/success; cursor pagination.
- E2E (Leila):
  - Navigate -> table loads
  - Apply filters -> request canceled/replaced correctly
  - Click route -> route detail page opens and filter params preserved

Rollout plan (this ticket)
- Land behind feature flag; dogfood on staging for internal orgs.
- Provide screenshots for docs (Elliot/Wei) once UI is stable.

Open questions
- Sparkline data source: do we include it in list response or request separately? (Prefer: include small time-bucketed series in list response if cheap; otherwise omit sparkline for v1.)
- Should model filter exist on list page in v1, or only in route detail? (Pending backend capability + PM decision.)
